labels.notes: Unmarked and partial, which is right for a claim refuted as printed. FINDING CHECKED, TRUE. (1) Statement. KBorelienAsPrinted carries exactly the remark's standing hypotheses: M second countable, T2, with its Borel σ-algebra (BorelSpace), a causality, tarentin, and any p. Its conclusion is MeasurableSet (C.Kminus ⊤ {p}). Causality.Kminus (Causal/Reachable.lean:98) is defi:futur_continue verbatim: ⋂ over sequences u → p of ⋃_N Int_{J^-(p)}(J^-(p) ∩ ⋂_{n≥N} J^-(u n)), where interiorWithin is the relative interior. Universe 0 is disclosed and harmless for a refutation. (2) The witness is a topological spacetime in the paper's sense. spokesCausality A fills every field of the library's Causality: (a) le_refl/le_trans, (b) le_mono/lt_mono, (c) le_of_lt, ≪ transitive, and ≪ open in every U. Its ≪ is staticLt on ℝ × ℂ, which is the chronological relation of E^{1,2} in each open set (ℂ has the Euclidean norm). The segment condition is consistent. rel.mono holds because a segment in V ⊆ U lies in U. rel.trans holds because the composite segment [c'c,1]·z is [c,1]·z ∪ c·[c',1]·z. le.trans holds because base relates two points of t = 0 only when they are equal, so two spokes compose into one. Gluing (kb/0014, kb/0019): the witness is absolutely minimal in the library's sense, the paper's def:topological_space_causality_absolutely with lem:union_causalite's generated precausality. This is the cosheaf form of the sheaf condition, the strongest locality the library expresses. I checked the subdivision: each sub-step starts at t(n+1)·z ∈ A (t(n+1) > 0, and A is a cone), and its segment [t n, t(n+1)]·z lies in V ⊓ O_i. Tarentin (Int J_M(p,q), with p,q in any neighbourhood) and causal (≤_M antisymmetric) are the paper's sentences. DEC-12(b) (within-component relations) is met, since ≪ comes from curves in U and spokes from segments in U. No ruling (DEC-6/11/12/13/14/20/21) constrains a causality further. (3) Slice computation, checked by hand. Take ‖z‖ ≥ 1 and suppose (0,z) ≤ p = (1,0). This forces a spoke chain whose first base step stays in the slice t = 0, so it is the identity and z ∈ A. Conversely, for z ∈ A with ‖z‖ > 1, every x ∈ J^-(p) ∩ {1 + |t| < ‖x‖} lies below o = (0,0) (a ≪-step to p would need ‖x‖ < 1 - t). For any u_n → p, o ≪ u_n eventually, by openness of I^+(o), so one N serves every point of the neighbourhood, as the definition requires. (4) Non-Borel. exists_not_measurableSet_real is a genuine cardinality proof: Borel(ℝ) is generated by the countable family of rational intervals, so it has at most 𝔠 members, while Set ℝ has 2^𝔠 (Cardinal.cantor). It has no sorry and uses the standard three axioms. Mathlib has no such lemma at this pin (grep), so the kb proposal is right. g(x) = (0, 2x + 2i) is continuous with ‖g x‖ ≥ 2, and g(x) ∈ coneOver T iff x ∈ T, so K^-(p) Borel implies T Borel. ℝ × ℂ carries Prod.instMeasurableSpace with Prod.borelSpace, which is the Borel σ-algebra (#synth). J^-(p) is not Borel either, because K^-(p) = J^-(p) ∩ O (measurableSet_Kminus). (5) Future form. The witness is the dual; dual.Kplus ⊤ {p} = Kminus ⊤ {p} holds by rfl (probe). (6) The rest. The wording finding ('open in J^±(p)' should read J^-(p)) is right and is already in the ledger. The true forms are correct and hide no hypothesis. FirstCountable and OpensMeasurableSpace follow from the paper's second countable and Borel, and the library's prop:tarentin_fort_K needs neither tarentin nor absolute minimality. The SCOPE's prose claim that off t = 0, J^-(p) is (I^-(p) ∪ I^-({0}×A)) ∪ {p} also checks. For x.1 < 0, x ≤ p iff x ≪ p or x ≪ a for some a ∈ {0}×A. For x.1 > 0, only x = p or x ≪ p. This agrees with the paper's own rem:mesure_bord, which says J^±(A) need not be Borel. 'The one place the remark is used' is right: \ref{rem:K_borelien} occurs nowhere, and K^-(p)'s measurability is used at l.1228 in prop:cont_ext_cont.

findings.what: Both printed-form Props quantify over every library Causality, non-local ones included (kb/0014). So not_kBorelienAsPrinted and not_kBorelienPlusAsPrinted alone refute the remark only for the library's wider class. Locality is recorded only in spokes_counterexample, and only for the past form. REPORT findings[0] says 'a local (absolutely minimal) and causal causality … the future form likewise (not_kBorelienPlusAsPrinted)'. No Lean statement says that the future witness, the dual of spokesCausality, is absolutely minimal or causal. The claim is TRUE: Causality.dual_absolutelyMinimal (Causal/Minimal.lean:61) and Causality.dual_isCausal (Causal/Properties.lean:184) give it in one line each. Nothing is false or over-certified. This is an evidence gap in what goes to the author.
findings.fix: Add `C.AbsolutelyMinimal → C.IsCausal →` to both Props. They are then stronger to refute, and the proofs go through with spokes_absolutelyMinimal, spokes_isCausal, dual_absolutelyMinimal.2 and dual_isCausal.2. Each not_… theorem alone then refutes the remark for local causal spacetimes. Alternatively, add a future-form companion to spokes_counterexample that records the dual's tarentin, IsCausal and AbsolutelyMinimal.
